"""
L2.1 - Town enrichment for voters_postgresql

Pipeline position:  L2  ->  L2.1  ->  L3
  - Reads the batch L2 wrote to voters_postgresql (already through fix_address_fields).
  - Makes sure the town / city is in address4 whenever address4 is empty. Nothing else is rearranged
    (the supplier does its own address shifting later).
  - Writes the result back to voters_postgresql; L3 then appends it to the Delta table as before.
  - Does not touch voters_transformed. Safe to re-run.

Postcodes missing from the national file take their town from the same postcode sector (CV78), then the
same district (CV7), so a new-build postcode still gets a town (and a2 = COVENTRY is recognised as the town).

Rules (lines considered: address2, address3, address4, address5; address and address6 are never changed)
  Duplicates:  address5 equal to address2/3/4, address3 equal to address4, address2 equal to address3/4
               -> the duplicate line is cleared (address4 is kept in preference to the others).
  Address4 empty / UNKNOWN:
     1. address5, address3 or address2 is the town (exact or near-match with the national names for the
        postcode)                          -> moved to address4, source line cleared, nothing else moves
     2. the town is already a line of its own somewhere (e.g. address1)   -> no change
     3. the town is nowhere in the row     -> the national town (a built-up-area name) is written to address4.
        A postcode that only has a district name, or a London borough (NEWHAM, CAMDEN...), is NOT filled.
        A London borough already in the row is not treated as the town either: it is left where it is.
  Address4 holds a value:
     4. it is the town (exact / near-match)                               -> no change
     5. the town is nowhere in the row, address5 is empty, address4 looks like a place (county, borough...,
        not a street / institution) and the national town is known         -> address4 moves to address5,
        the national town is written to address4
     6. anything else (institution, street, address5 also used, ...)      -> never touched
"""
from pyspark.sql import SparkSession, functions as F

spark = SparkSession.builder.getOrCreate()

# ---- CONFIG -----------------------------------------------------------
env = mssparkutils.env.getWorkspaceName().split("-")[-1]
STORAGE_ACCOUNT = f"baubaisadfsa{env}"
BASE = f"abfss://juror-etl@{STORAGE_ACCOUNT}.dfs.core.windows.net"
POSTGRES_PATH = f"{BASE}/voters_postgresql"
TMP_PATH = f"{BASE}/voters_postgresql_town_tmp"
BACKUP_PATH = f"{BASE}/voters_postgresql_pre_town_backup"      # copy of the batch before enrichment (kept for one run)
LOOKUP_PATH = f"{BASE}/reference/postcode_town_lookup"

NATIONAL_CSV_PATH = f"abfss://dl-juror-eric-voters-temp@{STORAGE_ACCOUNT}.dfs.core.windows.net/postcodes.csv"
NATIONAL_SEP = ","                                             # "\t" if tab-separated
NATIONAL_POSTCODE_COL = "Postcode"
TOWN_COLS_PRIORITY = ["Built up area", "District"]             # first non-blank becomes the town written to address4
# Names that count as "this is the town". County / Region / Constituency / Local authority are left out on purpose.
TOWN_NAME_COLS = ["Built up area", "District", "Ward", "Parish"]

POSTCODE_COL = "zip"
LINES = ["address", "address2", "address3", "address4", "address5", "address6"]   # searched for the town
MAX_LEN = 35
FUZZY_MIN_LEN = 8         # near-match (typo) check only for names at least this long
FUZZY_MAX_DIST = 2        # max Levenshtein distance (whole address line vs a name) for names of 8-9 letters
FUZZY_LONG_LEN = 10       # names this long or longer may differ by one more letter
FUZZY_MAX_DIST_LONG = 3
# London boroughs are NOT towns: never filled from the postcode, never moved (the postal town is LONDON).
# Boroughs that are also real postal towns (BROMLEY, CROYDON, HARROW, ENFIELD, SUTTON, KINGSTON UPON THAMES,
# HOUNSLOW, BARNET) are deliberately not in this list.
LONDON_BOROUGHS = ["BARKING AND DAGENHAM", "BEXLEY", "BRENT", "CAMDEN", "EALING", "GREENWICH", "HACKNEY",
                   "HAMMERSMITH AND FULHAM", "HARINGEY", "HAVERING", "HILLINGDON", "ISLINGTON",
                   "KENSINGTON AND CHELSEA", "LAMBETH", "LEWISHAM", "MERTON", "NEWHAM", "REDBRIDGE",
                   "RICHMOND UPON THAMES", "SOUTHWARK", "TOWER HAMLETS", "WALTHAM FOREST", "WANDSWORTH",
                   "WESTMINSTER"]
# rule 5: an address4 value containing one of these words is a street / building, never pushed to address5
PUSH_BLOCK_REGEX = (r"(^| )(ROAD|RD|STREET|LANE|AVENUE|DRIVE|CLOSE|CRESCENT|TERRACE|SQUARE|HOUSE|HALL|HALLS|FARM|"
                    r"COTTAGE|COTTAGES|MANOR|CENTRE|CENTER|HOME|FLATS|APARTMENTS|ESTATE|LODGE|COURT)( |$)")
# A line that ends in / contains one of these is a street, building or institution, not a locality
STREET_END_REGEX = (r"(^| )(ROAD|RD|STREET|ST|LANE|LN|AVENUE|AVE|DRIVE|DR|CLOSE|WAY|GARDENS|GROVE|CRESCENT|COURT|TERRACE|"
                    r"SQUARE|PLACE|RISE|VIEW|MEWS|PARADE|WALK|ROW|HOUSE|HALL|HALLS|LODGE|FARM|COTTAGE|COTTAGES|MANOR|"
                    r"CENTRE|CENTER|HOME|BUILDINGS|FLATS|APARTMENTS|ESTATE)( NORTH| SOUTH| EAST| WEST)?$")
NONLOCALITY_REGEX = (r"(^| )(UNIVERSITY|COLLEGE|SCHOOL|HOSPITAL|BARRACKS|RESIDENCE|PRISON|ACADEMY|CAMPUS)( |$)|"
                     r"^(FLAT|APARTMENT|APT|UNIT|BLOCK|ROOM|FLOOR|SUITE|PLOT) |[0-9]")
REBUILD_LOOKUP = False
DRY_RUN = False            # True = report only, nothing is written. Set False to write.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------

AFFIX_REGEX = (r"^(CITY OF|LONDON BOROUGH OF|ROYAL BOROUGH OF|COUNTY OF|GREATER|THE)\s+"
               r"|\s+(CITY|COUNTY|DISTRICT|BOROUGH|COUNCIL)$")
INSERT_AFFIX_REGEX = (r"^(CITY OF|LONDON BOROUGH OF|ROYAL BOROUGH OF|COUNTY OF|GREATER)\s+"
                      r"|\s+(CITY|COUNTY|DISTRICT|BOROUGH|COUNCIL)$")


def is_blank(col):
    return col.isNull() | (F.trim(col.cast("string")) == "")


def norm_pc(col):
    return F.regexp_replace(F.upper(col.cast("string")), r"[^A-Z0-9]", "")


def norm_text(col):
    s = F.regexp_replace(F.upper(F.coalesce(col.cast("string"), F.lit(""))), r"['’`]", "")   # ANNE'S -> ANNES
    t = F.regexp_replace(s, r"[^A-Z0-9]+", " ")
    return F.concat(F.lit(" "), F.trim(t), F.lit(" "))


def names_expr(cols):
    """Upper-case names from the columns, composite names split on '/', plus each name without common affixes."""
    parts = F.flatten(F.transform(
        F.array(*[F.upper(F.trim(F.col(f"`{c}`"))) for c in cols]),
        lambda x: F.split(F.coalesce(x, F.lit("")), "/")))
    base = F.filter(F.transform(parts, lambda x: F.trim(x)), lambda x: x != "")
    short = F.transform(base, lambda x: F.trim(F.regexp_replace(x, AFFIX_REGEX, "")))
    return F.filter(F.array_distinct(F.concat(base, short)), lambda x: x != "")


def delta_exists(path):
    try:
        spark.read.format("delta").load(path).limit(1).count()
        return True
    except Exception:
        return False


def build_lookup():
    raw = spark.read.option("header", True).option("sep", NATIONAL_SEP).csv(NATIONAL_CSV_PATH)
    make_lookup_df(raw).write.format("delta").mode("overwrite").option("overwriteSchema", "true").save(LOOKUP_PATH)


def make_lookup_df(raw):
    """Lookup rows at three levels: full postcode (town + every name that counts as the town), and the
    postcode sector (CV78) / district (CV7) with just the most common town. The coarser levels are used
    when a postcode is missing from the national file (new build postcodes)."""
    prio = [c for c in TOWN_COLS_PRIORITY if c in raw.columns]
    tcols = [c for c in TOWN_NAME_COLS if c in raw.columns]
    missing = [c for c in TOWN_COLS_PRIORITY + TOWN_NAME_COLS if c not in raw.columns]
    if missing:
        print(f"WARNING: columns not found in the national file (skipped): {sorted(set(missing))}")
    if not prio or not tcols:
        raise ValueError(f"Expected columns missing. File has: {raw.columns}")
    town_raw = F.coalesce(*[F.when(~is_blank(F.col(f"`{c}`")), F.upper(F.trim(F.col(f"`{c}`")))) for c in prio])
    town_clean = F.trim(F.regexp_replace(F.split(town_raw, "/").getItem(0), INSERT_AFFIX_REGEX, ""))
    town_clean = F.trim(F.regexp_replace(town_clean, r"\s*\(.*\)\s*", " "))          # LEIGH (WIGAN) -> LEIGH
    town = F.when(F.length(town_clean) > 0, town_clean)
    from_bua = F.when(~is_blank(F.col(f"`{prio[0]}`")), 1).otherwise(0)       # town came from the first (preferred) column
    base = (raw.select(norm_pc(F.col(f"`{NATIONAL_POSTCODE_COL}`")).alias("pc_norm"),
                       town.alias("town"), from_bua.alias("from_bua"), names_expr(tcols).alias("names"))
               .filter(F.length("pc_norm") >= 5)
               .withColumn("pc_sector", F.expr("substring(pc_norm, 1, length(pc_norm) - 2)"))
               .withColumn("pc_district", F.expr("substring(pc_norm, 1, length(pc_norm) - 3)")))

    def mode_town(key):                       # built-up-area names first, then the most common (ties alphabetical = deterministic)
        return (base.filter(F.col("town").isNotNull()).groupBy(key, "town", "from_bua").count()
                    .groupBy(key).agg(F.max(F.struct("from_bua", "count", "town")).alias("m"))
                    .select(F.col(key).alias("key"), F.col("m.town").alias("town"), F.col("m.from_bua").alias("town_bua")))

    names = (base.groupBy("pc_norm").agg(F.array_distinct(F.flatten(F.collect_set("names"))).alias("town_names"))
                 .withColumnRenamed("pc_norm", "key"))
    full = (names.join(mode_town("pc_norm"), "key", "left")
                 .select("key", "town", "town_bua", "town_names").withColumn("level", F.lit("full")))
    coarse = [mode_town(k).withColumn("town_names", F.array("town")).withColumn("level", F.lit(lv))
              .select("key", "town", "town_bua", "town_names", "level")
              for k, lv in [("pc_sector", "sector"), ("pc_district", "district")]]
    return full.unionByName(coarse[0]).unionByName(coarse[1])


def lookup_ready():
    """True when the saved lookup exists and has the current layout (key / level / town_bua columns)."""
    try:
        cols = spark.read.format("delta").load(LOOKUP_PATH).columns
        return "level" in cols and "town_bua" in cols
    except Exception:
        return False


def fuzzy_hit(line_col):
    """True when the whole (normalised) line is within a few edits of any known town name."""
    ln = F.trim(norm_text(line_col))
    return F.coalesce(
        F.exists("names_n", lambda t: (F.length(t) >= FUZZY_MIN_LEN) &
                 (F.levenshtein(ln, t) <= F.when(F.length(t) >= FUZZY_LONG_LEN, FUZZY_MAX_DIST_LONG).otherwise(FUZZY_MAX_DIST))),
        F.lit(False))


def exact_line(line_col):
    """True when the WHOLE (normalised) line equals a known town name. A street called COVENTRY ROAD does not count."""
    return F.coalesce(F.exists("names_n", lambda t: (F.length(t) > 0) & (F.trim(norm_text(line_col)) == t)), F.lit(False))


def enrich(df, lookup):
    """Returns the enriched DataFrame with helper columns kept (status, old_*, town) for reporting."""
    df = (df.withColumn("pc_norm", norm_pc(F.col(POSTCODE_COL)))
            .withColumn("pc_sector", F.expr("substring(pc_norm, 1, length(pc_norm) - 2)"))
            .withColumn("pc_district", F.expr("substring(pc_norm, 1, length(pc_norm) - 3)")))
    j = df
    for level, kc in [("full", "pc_norm"), ("sector", "pc_sector"), ("district", "pc_district")]:
        lk = (lookup.filter(F.col("level") == level)
                    .select(F.col("key").alias(kc), F.col("town").alias(f"town_{level}"),
                            F.col("town_bua").alias(f"bua_{level}"),
                            F.col("town_names").alias(f"names_{level}"))
                    .join(df.select(kc).distinct(), kc))                    # only this batch's postcodes
        j = j.join(lk, kc, "left")
    j = (j.withColumn("town", F.coalesce("town_full", "town_sector", "town_district"))
          .withColumn("town_names", F.coalesce("names_full", "names_sector", "names_district"))
          .withColumn("town_is_bua", F.coalesce("bua_full", "bua_sector", "bua_district"))   # 1 = built-up-area name, 0 = district / borough
          .withColumn("town_level", F.when(F.col("town_full").isNotNull(), "full")
                                     .when(F.col("town_sector").isNotNull(), "sector")
                                     .when(F.col("town_district").isNotNull(), "district"))
          .drop("town_full", "town_sector", "town_district", "names_full", "names_sector", "names_district",
                "bua_full", "bua_sector", "bua_district", "pc_sector", "pc_district"))

    # ---- is the town already a line of its own somewhere in the row? (whole line, exact or near-match)
    j = j.withColumn("names_n", F.filter(F.array_union(F.transform("town_names", lambda t: F.trim(norm_text(t))),
                                                       F.array(F.trim(norm_text(F.col("town"))))),
                                         lambda t: ~t.isin(*LONDON_BOROUGHS)))     # boroughs are not towns
    ex, fz = exact_line(F.col(LINES[0])), fuzzy_hit(F.col(LINES[0]))
    for c in LINES[1:]:
        ex, fz = ex | exact_line(F.col(c)), fz | fuzzy_hit(F.col(c))
    j = j.withColumn("found", ex.cast("int")).withColumn("found_fuzzy", fz.cast("int"))
    is_found, is_fuzzy, has_town = F.col("found") == 1, F.col("found_fuzzy") == 1, F.col("town").isNotNull()

    # ---- per-line facts (address2, 3, 4, 5)
    def real(c):                      # usable line: not blank, not the UNKNOWN placeholder, not NAN/NULL/NA
        return (~is_blank(F.col(c))) & (~F.upper(F.trim(F.col(c))).isin("UNKNOWN", "NAN", "NULL", "NA"))

    def n(c):
        return F.trim(norm_text(F.col(c)))

    def is_town_line(c):              # the WHOLE line is the town: equal to a known name once normalised, or a near-match
        return exact_line(F.col(c)) | fuzzy_hit(F.col(c))

    def locality_like(c):             # not a street / building / institution, no digits
        return real(c) & ~n(c).rlike(STREET_END_REGEX) & ~n(c).rlike(NONLOCALITY_REGEX)

    r2, r3, r4, r5 = real("address2"), real("address3"), real("address4"), real("address5")

    # duplicates: address4 wins over address3 / address2 / address5; address3 wins over address2
    clear5 = r5 & ((r2 & (n("address5") == n("address2"))) | (r3 & (n("address5") == n("address3"))) |
                   (r4 & (n("address5") == n("address4"))))
    clear3 = r3 & r4 & (n("address3") == n("address4"))
    clear2 = r2 & ((r3 & (n("address2") == n("address3"))) | (r4 & (n("address2") == n("address4"))))
    e2, e3, e5 = r2 & ~clear2, r3 & ~clear3, r5 & ~clear5          # lines that survive the duplicate clean-up

    m5, m3, m2 = e5 & is_town_line("address5"), e3 & is_town_line("address3"), e2 & is_town_line("address2")
    town_seen = is_found | is_fuzzy          # the town is somewhere in the row already
    real_town = (has_town & (F.col("town_is_bua") == 1)                         # a built-up-area name, not a district
                 & ~F.trim(norm_text(F.col("town"))).isin(*LONDON_BOROUGHS))    # and not a London borough
    src = F.when(~r4, F.when(m5, "address5").when(m3, "address3").when(m2, "address2"))     # rule 1
    push = (r4 & ~e5 & ~town_seen & real_town & locality_like("address4")
            & ~n("address4").rlike(PUSH_BLOCK_REGEX))                                        # rule 5

    status = (F.when(r4 & is_found, "already_present")
               .when(r4 & is_fuzzy, "already_present_fuzzy")                 # same town, spelt slightly differently
               .when(push, "pushed_to_address5")
               .when(r4, "address4_occupied")                                # never touched
               .when(src == "address5", "moved_from_address5")
               .when(src.isNotNull(), "moved_to_address4")
               .when(is_found, "already_present")                            # town in a longer line / address line 1
               .when(is_fuzzy, "already_present_fuzzy")
               .when(real_town, "filled")                                    # nothing usable -> national town
               .when(has_town, "district_only")                              # only a district / borough name known: not filled
               .otherwise("no_lookup_name"))

    for c in ["address2", "address3", "address4", "address5"]:
        j = j.withColumn(f"old_{c}", F.col(c))
    j = (j.withColumn("_src", src)
          .withColumn("_c2", clear2).withColumn("_c3", clear3).withColumn("_c5", clear5)
          .withColumn("_v2", F.trim(F.col("address2"))).withColumn("_v3", F.trim(F.col("address3")))
          .withColumn("_v4", F.trim(F.col("address4"))).withColumn("_v5", F.trim(F.col("address5")))
          .withColumn("status", status)
          .withColumn("dup_cleared", (clear2 | clear3 | clear5).cast("int")))
    st, s = F.col("status"), F.col("_src")
    none = F.lit(None).cast("string")
    moved = st.isin("moved_from_address5", "moved_to_address4")
    j = (j.withColumn("address4", F.when(moved & (s == "address5"), F.col("_v5"))
                                   .when(moved & (s == "address3"), F.col("_v3"))
                                   .when(moved & (s == "address2"), F.col("_v2"))
                                   .when(st.isin("filled", "pushed_to_address5"), F.substring(F.col("town"), 1, MAX_LEN))
                                   .otherwise(F.col("address4")))
          .withColumn("address2", F.when(F.col("_c2") | (moved & (s == "address2")), none).otherwise(F.col("address2")))
          .withColumn("address3", F.when(F.col("_c3") | (moved & (s == "address3")), none).otherwise(F.col("address3")))
          .withColumn("address5", F.when(st == "pushed_to_address5", F.col("_v4"))
                                   .when(F.col("_c5") | (moved & (s == "address5")), none).otherwise(F.col("address5")))
          .drop("_src", "_c2", "_c3", "_c5", "_v2", "_v3", "_v4", "_v5"))
    return j


def main():
    if REBUILD_LOOKUP or not lookup_ready():
        print("Building postcode lookup (runs once)...")
        build_lookup()
    lookup = spark.read.format("delta").load(LOOKUP_PATH)

    df = spark.read.parquet(POSTGRES_PATH)
    orig_cols = df.columns
    orig_count = df.count()
    if orig_count == 0:
        print("voters_postgresql is empty: nothing to enrich, nothing changed.")
        return
    print(f"voters_postgresql batch: {orig_count:,} rows")

    j = enrich(df, lookup).cache()
    print("=== Outcome ===")
    (j.groupBy("status").count()
      .withColumn("pct", F.round(F.col("count") * 100.0 / orig_count, 2)).orderBy("status").show(truncate=False))
    print("Rows where a duplicate line was cleared:", j.filter("dup_cleared = 1").count())
    print("=== Sample of changed rows (old -> new) ===")
    (j.filter(F.col("status").isin("filled", "moved_from_address5", "moved_to_address4", "pushed_to_address5"))
      .select("status", "address", "old_address2", "old_address3", "old_address4", "old_address5",
              "address2", "address3", "address4", "address5", POSTCODE_COL).limit(20).show(truncate=False))

    if DRY_RUN:
        print("DRY_RUN = True: nothing written.")
        return

    from notebookutils import mssparkutils            # Synapse only
    out = j.select(*orig_cols)
    writer = out.write.mode("overwrite")
    if "creation_date_partition" in orig_cols:
        writer = writer.partitionBy("creation_date_partition")
    writer.parquet(TMP_PATH)                          # never overwrite the path we are reading from

    new_count = spark.read.parquet(TMP_PATH).count()
    if new_count != orig_count:
        raise RuntimeError(f"Row count changed ({orig_count} -> {new_count}); voters_postgresql left untouched.")

    if mssparkutils.fs.exists(BACKUP_PATH):
        mssparkutils.fs.rm(BACKUP_PATH, True)
    mssparkutils.fs.mv(POSTGRES_PATH, BACKUP_PATH)
    mssparkutils.fs.mv(TMP_PATH, POSTGRES_PATH)
    print(f"voters_postgresql updated ({new_count:,} rows). Previous version kept at {BACKUP_PATH}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
